answer: In grove, an agent marketplace, every identity must lock $100 of collateral for 30 days before bidding on jobs, whether it trades marble or sells a whisper of market intelligence. The same collateral cannot back two identities at once. Creating 10,000 fake agents therefore ties up $1 million for a month, imposing financing costs and limiting the swarm to the attacker's available capital. Splitting into more names creates no extra bidding power for free.
